Quatre jours pour travailler

Depuis un an, les trente salariés de Clic & Colis, une petite entreprise nantaise qui prépare des colis pour des boutiques en ligne, ne travaillent plus que quatre jours par semaine. … L'idée vient de la directrice, Sophie Guérin. « Nos employés étaient fatigués, beaucoup étaient souvent malades, et nous avions du mal à recruter », explique-t-elle.

Sophie Guérin a voulu changer l'organisation du travail parce que…

  1. ses employés étaient souvent fatigués et malades.
  2. ses clients n'étaient pas satisfaits.
  3. son entreprise perdait de l'argent.

The exams

What the written tests ask, level by level

The DELF (Diplôme d'études en langue française, A1 to B2) and the DALF (Diplôme approfondi de langue française, C1 and C2) are diplomas of the French Ministry of Education, made by France Éducation international. Each level is a separate exam, and the diploma is valid for life. Every level also has a speaking test, which Glossa's papers do not include.

The TCF (Test de connaissance du français) is made by France Éducation international too, but has no levels to choose from: one test places you on a level from A1 to C2. Glossa's papers follow the general version, the TCF tout public.

ExamThe real written testsIn Glossa's papers
DELF A1Listening (about 20 minutes, 21 items), reading (30 minutes, 20 items) and writing: a form and a message of at least 40 words (30 minutes).The same task types with about half the items: listening 10 minutes, reading 15 minutes. Writing at full length, 30 minutes.
DELF A2Listening (25 minutes, 22 items), reading (30 minutes, 23 items) and two texts of at least 60 words each (45 minutes).Listening 14 minutes and reading 17 minutes, with about half the items. Writing at full length, 45 minutes.
DELF B1Listening (about 25 minutes, 20 items), reading (45 minutes) and one opinion text of at least 160 words (45 minutes).Listening 13 minutes and reading 24 minutes, with about half the questions. Writing at full length, 45 minutes.
DELF B2Listening (about 30 minutes, 20 items), reading (1 hour) and one argued text of at least 250 words (1 hour).Listening 17 minutes and reading 33 minutes, with about half the questions. Writing at full length, 1 hour.
DALF C1Listening (about 40 minutes, 17 items), one text of about 1,000 words with 12 items (50 minutes), and a synthesis of documents plus an argued essay (2 hours 30 minutes).9 listening items in 21 minutes and 6 reading items on a full-length text in 25 minutes. Writing at full length, 2 hours 30 minutes.
DALF C2Reading and writing: one structured text of at least 700 words from a dossier of about 2,000 words (3 hours 30 minutes). Listening and speaking are a separate, individual test.The reading-and-writing test at full length, 3 hours 30 minutes. No listening-and-speaking test.
TCF tout publicListening (25 minutes, 29 questions), language structures (15 minutes, 18 questions) and reading (45 minutes, 29 questions), plus optional writing (3 tasks, 60 minutes) and speaking.Listening 13 minutes, language structures 8 minutes and reading 23 minutes, with about half the questions. Writing at full length, 60 minutes, in every paper.
TCF IRNFour compulsory tests in one session: listening (20 minutes, 25 questions), reading (35 minutes, 25 questions), writing (3 tasks, 30 minutes) and speaking with an examiner (10 minutes). No language structures test.Listening 10 minutes and reading 18 minutes, with about half the questions. Writing at full length, 30 minutes. No speaking.

Based on France Éducation international's published exam descriptions and sample papers and the TCF candidate's manual, checked in October 2026. Check them for the current format.

Results

How the exams are passed or scored

  • DELF A1 to DALF C1: four tests of 25 points each. You pass with at least 50 of the 100 points and at least 5 of 25 in each test, so a strong test can make up for a weaker one, but a test below 5 fails the exam.
  • DALF C2: two tests of 50 points each. You pass with at least 50 of the 100 points and at least 10 of 50 in each test.
  • TCF: there is no pass or fail. Each test places you on a level from A1 to C2, and whether that is enough depends on the level the university, employer or authority asks for. The certificate is valid for two years.
  • TCF IRN: no pass or fail either. Listening and reading each get a score from 100 to 499 and writing and speaking a mark out of 20, each with a level from A1 to B2, and the certificate is valid for two years. Whether a result is enough depends on the level the prefecture asks for.

Residence and nationality

Which level the TCF IRN must show

The TCF IRN (Test de connaissance du français – Intégration, Résidence et Nationalité) is for people living in France who must prove their French to the authorities. Since 1 January 2026, these levels apply in writing and speaking (for the residence cards, to non-EU applicants under 65 applying for a first card):

ApplicationLevel
A first multi-year residence card (carte de séjour pluriannuelle)A2
A first resident card, long-term resident–EU card or permanent resident cardB1
Naturalisation by decree, reinstatement, or a declaration of nationality by marriageB2

Before 1 January 2026 the resident card needed A2 and naturalisation B1; nationality applications filed before that date keep the old rules. The authorities name the TCF and the TEF; certain diplomas count instead of a test, and only the prefecture grants exemptions. First residence cards and naturalisation also need a separate civic exam on France, which is not a language test and which Glossa does not practise. Check service-public.gouv.fr for your own case.

Honest limits

How the practice papers differ from the real exams

  • No grade, score or level is given. A paper shows your share of the points. It applies the DELF and DALF pass rule to the tests it has, but cannot tell you what you would score in the real exam, and a TCF paper is not converted into a score from 100 to 699 (100 to 499 for the TCF IRN) or a level.
  • Listening and reading are shorter, with about half the items and the time cut to match. The writing is full length.
  • There is no speaking test at any level, and no listening-and-speaking test at C2. Glossa cannot assess free speech the way examiners do.
  • The TCF and TCF IRN papers are not adaptive or weighted. The questions get harder as you go, as in the real test, but every question counts the same.
  • Recordings can be replayed. In the real exams you hear each recording once or twice, depending on the task; listen that many times and then answer.
  • One voice per recording. In dialogues and interviews both speakers are read by one voice, with their names or roles.

Questions

Common questions

Is Glossa an official DELF or TCF preparation course?
No. Glossa is not connected with France Éducation international or the French Ministry of Education. The papers follow their published exam descriptions, with original content.
Which exam should I practise for?
The one the school, employer or authority asks for. The DELF and DALF are taken at one level you choose and are valid for life; the TCF places you on a level and its certificate is valid for two years. For a residence card or French nationality, the TCF IRN is the version of the TCF made for it.
What is free?
The whole French course from A1 to C1, the grammar reference and word practice are free. The practice papers, conversation practice, stories and the other extras are part of Premium.
I speak Finnish, German, Russian or Ukrainian. Is there a course for me?
Yes. French for Finnish, German, Russian and Ukrainian speakers have the same DELF, DALF, TCF and TCF IRN papers, with the instructions and explanations in that language.
